question: A 2-year-old boy (weight 12 kg) is diagnosed with iron deficiency anaemia. You prescribe oral elemental iron therapy. What is the correct therapeutic dose?

answers.text: 1–2 mg/kg/day elemental iron in 2–3 divided doses

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is below the therapeutic dose for IDA. The prophylactic dose for at-risk infants is around 1–2 mg/kg/day, but a child with established IDA needs 3–6 mg/kg/day elemental iron.

answers.text: 3–6 mg/kg/day elemental iron in 2–3 divided doses

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The therapeutic dose for IDA in children is 3–6 mg/kg/day elemental iron given in 2–3 divided doses, continued for 3 months after Hb normalises to replenish iron stores.

answers.text: 10–12 mg/kg/day elemental iron as a single dose

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This dose is excessive and increases the risk of GI side-effects (nausea, vomiting, constipation). The correct dose is 3–6 mg/kg/day in divided doses.

answers.text: 2 mg/kg once weekly as per the National Anaemia Control Programme schedule

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Weekly supplementation schedules apply to prophylaxis under national programmes, not to treatment of established IDA. Treatment requires daily therapeutic dosing at 3–6 mg/kg/day.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: therapeutic iron for IDA in children is 3–6 mg/kg/day elemental iron. Prophylactic doses and weekly supplementation schedules are lower and used for different purposes.
Correct! Therapeutic oral iron for IDA = 3–6 mg/kg/day elemental iron in 2–3 divided doses, continued for 3 months post-Hb recovery to replenish stores.
